rv.q: Third Rail’s effective and engaging evocation of life in the theater is such a terrific idea that they could take it on the road.
So tell me, what theatergoer wouldn’t be enticed by a backstage pass to this opulent venue, seasoned with just a touch of the supernatural?
Morris and Willett's most impressive feat is the coordination of several overlapping scenes

cn.t: Critics are split on Third Rail Projects' immersive "Ghost Light" at Lincoln Center — some find it enchanting theater magic, others fault its muddled script. The atmospheric staging earns praise, but weak dramaturgy holds it back.
